paragraphs.literal_text: The named encounter supplies a subject rather than a complete explanation. C003 distinguishes Prenapates' presence from an abductor allegation and from OS authentication, control and timer reports. Those pieces of evidence have different owners and functions. An allegation can make the encounter consequential without becoming a fully staged history; a system reading can constrain a situation without disclosing the intention behind every act. The reader should therefore resist making a recognizable enemy role do the work of an already known biography. The particular person remains worth asking about precisely where that role leaves questions unanswered. [C003:44,53,56,62–63]

paragraphs.literal_text: Counterpart recognition strengthens that inquiry without making the two teachers interchangeable. C004 supplies familiar Arona biometric support, and the two-card encounter includes participant identification of Prenapates as another Sensei. This is positive local evidence, not merely resemblance supplied by an analyst. It does not establish numerical identity, symmetric memories, the same motives or a complete account of the body through which Prenapates is encountered. The comparison can remain useful without turning current Sensei's clearly attributed choices into facts about the other teacher. [C004:30; E006:26,30]
